blocks.note: first meaning: Old Scratch is a nickname for the Devil
second meaning: an old name for a friction match

explanation.surface: Someone calls off a fixture at the last minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scratch the match' reads as cancelling a game; in fact both words are separate names for one thing: Old Scratch is the Devil, and a lucifer was an early match.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucifer is the fallen angel, the Devil, also called Old Scratch; Victorian strike-anywhere matches were sold as lucifers.

clue.text: Supple plant written up in fiction

one word is placed inside the other, sitting within it

blocks.note: a lie is a fiction
moss is a small plant

explanation.surface: A flexible plant appears in a novel, described upside-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Lissome describes a body that is slender and flexible, bending easily, which is what supple means.

indicators.note: the beasts catch and hold something between them, enclosing it
the name is wrapped around the number, which sits inside it

blocks.note: beasts taken as two cats
Chas is the short form of Charles
taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: Animals ensnare the fictional detective Charlie Chan amid a wrestling free-for-all.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie Chan was a fictional detective; here Charlie is Chas. All-in wrestling is a British term for a style with almost no holds barred.
explanation.definitionFit: Catch-as-catch-can is a freestyle wrestling style in which nearly any hold is permitted, the same as all-in wrestling.

indicators.note: something knocked out of shape has its parts rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A meerkat has had the stuffing knocked out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'knock the stuffing out of' hides that 'Stuffing' is the definition and 'knocked out' the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Forcemeat is a seasoned mixture of chopped meat or breadcrumbs used to fill poultry before cooking.

clue.text: Say, one to five in operation

blocks.note: the letters sit inside this word

explanation.surface: A surgeon estimates odds of one in five that an operation will succeed.
explanation.definitionFit: One to five expresses a proportion between two quantities, so it is an example of such a comparison.

indicators.note: to feature something is to include it, so the first word holds the second

blocks.note: to shock or horrify
RE means concerning, about

explanation.surface: A scandalous outfit is the talk of the fashion pages.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is clothing in general, so it is a synonym for dress used as a collective noun.

clue.text: A sound declaration of intended reconciliation

blocks.note: taken as written
a tone is a sound
meant means intended

explanation.surface: A firm statement of intent to make up after a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonement originally meant being at one, so it is the restoring of harmony between estranged parties.

clue.text: Cub takes work that arises by itself

blocks.note: a young animal
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A young Scout accepts a job that turns up on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A pop-up item, like a toaster's slice or a book's cutout, springs upward of its own accord.

blocks.note: surface reading: what an engineer is sketching in a technical drawing
setter's reading: what an engine driver's locomotive pulls along the track

explanation.surface: A draughtsman sketches the object of an engineering project.
explanation.walkthrough: A line drawing is a sketch, but here the engine draws (pulls) a vehicle along the line (track); engineer is the old word for an engine driver.
explanation.definitionFit: A passenger vehicle hauled by a locomotive over the tracks is exactly what a train engine pulls along.

clue.text: Coming after a little opening to the side

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its very beginning, its initial letter

blocks.note: later means following in time
taken as written
the first letter of little

explanation.surface: Someone follows through a narrow gap off to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral describes something situated at or directed sideways, as in lateral movement, away from the centre.

blocks.note: surface reading: the point at which a hill or slope becomes steep enough to climb
setter's reading: steep as a verb, to soak something in liquid until it can absorb no more

explanation.surface: A climber talks about the height at which the ground turns sharply upward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steep' looks like an adjective about a slope; it is the verb meaning soak, and you soak something until it holds no more liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: When you soak a material thoroughly, the stage at which it absorbs nothing further is its limit of absorption.

clue.text: Yellow's right in the firing line

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits inside the line, within its letters

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
the oche is the line darts players throw from

explanation.surface: A coward is accused of cowering when placed at the front of the battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Yellow suggests cowardice under fire, but it is the colour; the firing line is the darts oche, the mark behind which a player stands to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy pigment ranging from pale to brownish yellow, so the colour name fits.

a debtor is one who owes, an ower

clue.text: Put tight cover on ex-PM in quarters

blocks.note: the compass points East, North, South and East divide the compass into quarters
Edward Heath, British Prime Minister 1970 to 1974

explanation.walkthrough: Ted Heath was Britain's Conservative Prime Minister in the early 1970s; quarters here are the compass points, not lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensheathe is to enclose in a sheath, a close-fitting casing, so it means wrapping something snugly.

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fabric's heat-resistance figure is measured before being put under the grill.
explanation.walkthrough: A tog rating is the British measure of how warm a duvet or quilt is.
explanation.definitionFit: The tog is a unit of thermal resistance, so a duvet's tog figure states how well its fabric keeps heat in.

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A metallurgist remarks that a genuine alloy is a blend of metals.
explanation.definitionFit: True in the sense of faithful, as in a true friend, describes someone steadfast in allegiance.

clue.text: 'E's out to leach rye meal of drops

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cockney explains he has gone out to wash rye flour through.
explanation.walkthrough: ''E's out' reads as Cockney for 'he is out'; it tells you to remove every E from the words that follow, and the rest reads straight off in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Lachrymal relates to tears, the drops shed from the eyes, so 'of drops' is a playful gloss.

blocks.note: first meaning: a vessel

explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen makes it look like one activity, boat-building; split it and you get a vessel, and a skilled trade exemplified by building.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a vessel, as in small craft, and also a skilled manual trade such as carpentry or building.

clue.text: Short description of Princess Anne's body?

sister, shortened to sis, completes the description

explanation.surface: A tabloid offers a brief account of the Princess Royal's figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Anne is Charles's sister: shorten both words and you get Chas sis. The Princess Royal is the late Queen's only daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A chassis is the frame or bodywork of a vehicle, so body fits in the motoring sense.

clue.text: Riot at charges to get in?

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Protesters riot over admission fees so they can force their way into an event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riot' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is a command to scramble the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To gatecrash is to get into a party or event without an invitation or ticket; the question mark flags the loose sense.

blocks.note: first meaning: the surname of the jazz singer Billie ...
second meaning: a break from work or school

clue.text: A circular unit's housing 100 idyllic peasants

radians are the units for measuring angles round a circle

explanation.walkthrough: A circular unit sounds like a round building; it is the radian, the unit of angle.

blocks.note: the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fields' looks like part of the rural scene; it means holds, so the answer is held in the words before it, read backwards.

clue.text: What O is, if M is head of MI5?

definitions.text: What O is, if M is head of MI5?

blocks.clueFragment: What O is, if M is head of MI5?
blocks.note: surface reading: in Bond films M heads the secret service, so the next letter, O, would be the deputy
setter's reading: the letter O stands second in the word command

explanation.surface: A spy-fiction riddle about the ranking of lettered officials in the secret service.
explanation.walkthrough: If M heads the service, O is next in rank; and in the word 'command' the letter O does stand second.
